governs.note: Every edge in `edges` is a child dispatched through the routed adapter and validated at runtime by lib/child-inputs.py against its required_inputs/optional_inputs. This manifest governs that substrate and no other. The `orchestrator.*` and `sdd.*` edges are reachable ONLY on the non-default --backend=wezterm|background transports; since RFC 0015 the default /solve and /turbo route is the Workflow fleet declared under does_not_govern.

scope.agent_kind_rule: An agent kind is a Workflow agent's opts.label with `:#<issue>` and any trailing ` (<tier>)` removed, the per-task `:t<n>` and per-round `:r<n>` indices collapsed to `:tN` and `:rN`, then `:` mapped to `.` and `-` mapped to `_`. The indices are collapsed because they say which INSTANCE of a rung ran, not what it is: left in, a round-3 reviewer of task 12 is its own kind, the kind space is unbounded, and no enumeration below could satisfy C1 for a chain that actually runs. Derived by execution in tests/solve-run-tree-scope.test.sh, never by grep.

does_not_govern.reason: RFC 0015 made this the DEFAULT /solve + /turbo route. A Workflow script has no filesystem (tests/workflow-scripts.test.sh T1 forbids fs./process.), so it cannot read this manifest and no edge here can constrain it. The gap is real and tracked; it is recorded here so it is visible and machine-checked rather than inferred from a name.

RFC 0020 added /turbox as a SECOND lane off the same launcher: `--standard` pins the resolved backend to `workflow` and then emits a turbox plan instead of a Workflow args envelope, so the calling SESSION becomes the fleet orchestrator and dispatches every agent through the Task tool. It never sources lib/child-dispatch.sh, so it mints no instance id, creates no handoff, and produces no run-tree edge or receipt — it is neither the governed routed-child substrate nor the Workflow-native one above. RFC 0020 §1 positions this lane as the one that CAN run the parallel-wave implementation phase, so it is a candidate default; a default lane with zero run-tree governance and no declaration of that fact would let this manifest read as full coverage. Recorded here so the gap is visible and machine-checked (#649).
does_not_govern.agent_kind_rule: The rule in scope.agent_kind_rule normalizes a Workflow opts.label and cannot apply here: this lane runs no script, so there is no label to normalize and nothing to execute under the test harness. A kind is instead an agent identifier the source names — `uberdev:<stem>` where plugins/uberdev/agents/<stem>.md exists (which is what excludes the label `uberdev:active`, the command `uberdev:turbox` and the skill `uberdev:orchestrator`), plus the host built-in `general-purpose`, with `-` mapped to `_`. dispatch_sites is the number of such mentions rather than the number of distinct kinds: every one of them is a dispatch instruction, and `implementation-worker` is named at two of them (the Phase 4b wave implementer and the Phase 5 fix round). The Phase 6 delivery rung names no agent type at all, so it contributes no site. Derived from the source by C9 in tests/solve-run-tree-scope.test.sh, never by hand.

What makes THIS lane's gap real rather than nominal: it is the shared fixed-fleet engine behind TWO commands — /uberscan at mode=scan and /ubersimplify at mode=simplify — and unlike the read-only fleets it is a WRITING workflow: the apply arm dispatches one uberdev:code-fixer per area sequentially onto a shared branch, each committing, and the pr arm opens a PR. An ungoverned lane here mutates the repository and opens PRs, not just files issues. It also scales past any fixed edge list: numAreas clamps to 1..24 and each area costs a reviewer plus (in simplify) a fixer and a fixer-aggregate, with maxAgents clamping to 2000, so one run can dispatch far more agents than the twelve sites suggest. Because two commands enter one script, a name-based reading of coverage is doubly wrong — neither `uberscan.` nor `ubersimplify.` names the substrate — which is why the entry is keyed `scan_fleet.`, after the script rather than after either command, and recorded here so the gap is visible and machine-checked rather than inferred from a name (#654).

does_not_govern.reason: RFC 0015 §5 made /goal a Workflow-native driver: lib/goal-phase0.sh emits the args envelope and skills/goal-pipeline/workflow.js owns the cycle loop that used to live in five SKILL.md bash fences the orchestrating model was merely trusted to re-run in order. A Workflow script has no filesystem (RFC 0012 §2.2 constraint 6, enforced by tests/workflow-scripts.test.sh T1, which forbids fs./process.), so it cannot read this manifest and no edge here can constrain it. This lane's gap is the sharpest of the five, because its real fleet dispatch is not an agent() call at all: the four agent() sites are shell relays (claim, watch, verdicts, collect) and the run that actually solves a cycle is a nested `await workflow({ scriptPath: solveFleetJs }, fleetArgs)` at :884, built from the literal at :170. The test harness records that in record.workflowCalls and never in record.agentCalls, so a derivation keyed on agent labels alone certifies four shell relays as this lane's entire dispatch surface while the fleet run it exists to perform goes unrecorded — a manifest that reads as complete exactly where it is blind. That is why dispatch_sites counts 4 agent sites plus 1 workflow site, and why agent_kinds carries workflow.solve_fleet. RFC 0012 §2.2 constraint 7 bounds the nesting chase at one level, so the nested namespace is complete by construction rather than open-ended. Recorded here so the gap is visible and machine-checked (#654).

A kind here is therefore the label with both `:c<n>` and `:t<n>` collapsed to `:cN` and `:tN`, then `:` mapped to `.` and `-` mapped to `_`. This lane is the largest agent producer in the plugin — 21 dispatch sites against solve-fleet's 14 — and its fanout is combinatorial rather than fixed: islands x donors/generators, islands x synthesizer lenses x genetic rounds, islands x shortlist rows x falsifier lenses x rounds. One default two-island run dispatches 76 agents, and the whole of it is invisible to the routed-child adapter this manifest governs. Left undeclared, the manifest's silence about the biggest fanout in the repo reads as "nothing here dispatches", which is the false negative this entry exists to close. does_not_govern.agent_kind_rule: An agent kind in uberthink_pipeline is a Workflow agent's opts.label with every INSTANCE index collapsed and every script-declared literal kept, then `-` mapped to `_`. Five things collapse: the island index k becomes kN, the three-digit `pad(c + 1)` shortlist-row index becomes cN, the genetic round suffix `-r<n>` becomes rN, the scope gate's donor slug in `gen-<k>-<x>` becomes donor, and the moderator's gap id in `regen-<k>-<id>` becomes gap. Everything else is kept because it is a literal in the script's own bytes rather than an instance of one: the site prefixes gen- regen- moderator- synth- shortlist- falsify- frame-, the FRAME_LENSES / SYNTH_LENSES / FALSIFY_LENSES lens names, the four OPERATORS names, and the thirteen fixed labels. The indices are collapsed because they say which INSTANCE of a rung ran, not what it is: left in, island 2's second composite under the redteam lens in round 1 is its own kind, the kind space grows with --islands and with whatever donor catalog the scope gate returns, and no enumeration below could satisfy C1 for a run that actually happens. This lane is NOT the testers_pipeline grammar with a different id: it carries an island index and a pad() candidate index that lane has no notion of, which is why a rule copied across the two reds C12 on a missing index token.
